transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I’m just… exhausted. Not just normal tired, like after a long day, but like my whole body is full of wet sand or something. I work as a cashier, so I’m on my feet and trying to smile and pay attention to people and count change and all that, and lately I can barely get through a shift. By the time I’m standing there, even early on, I feel like I’m dragging myself from one minute to the next.

And I keep thinking if I just rest more, or sit down when I get home, or sleep it off, I’ll feel like myself again, but it doesn’t really bring me back. It’s like I’m still drained no matter what I do. I don’t know, it’s gotten to where I felt like I needed to talk to someone because I can’t keep pretending I’m just a little tired.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say “depressed” exactly, because that word feels kind of big, but I’ve definitely been feeling… flat, I guess. Like things that normally make me feel like me just don’t really do anything right now.

I usually like cooking for myself — not fancy or anything, but I like picking something out and chopping things and making it nice — and lately it just feels like this huge pointless chore. I’ll think about making something I used to enjoy and then it’s like, why bother? Same with playing guitar. I’ll pick it up and hold it for a minute, and I’m not even really interested in the sound of it. It’s like I’m pretending I still care.

Even hiking, which usually clears my head, just seems… empty. And going to my family’s place, which I normally look forward to, feels more like I’m acting normal than actually enjoying being there. I still go through the motions sometimes, but inside it’s like everything has the color turned down.
After even small amounts of physical or mental effort, do you feel markedly worse afterward?

Yeah, definitely. Even little things feel like they take way more out of me than they should. Like at work, I’m just standing there at the register, scanning things, answering simple questions, counting change — stuff I’ve done a million times — but it feels like I’m hauling my body through mud the whole time.

And then afterward I’m not just “oh, I had a busy day” tired. It’s like I crash. My whole body feels heavy, like I said, almost like it’s packed with wet sand, and my brain feels worn out too. I keep thinking if I just sit down for a while or sleep more, I’ll bounce back, but I don’t really. Rest helps maybe a tiny bit in the moment, but it doesn’t bring me back to normal. I still feel drained, like I’m running on almost nothing.
For the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling sad or hopeless most of the day?

I’m not really sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I’ve felt low and kind of worn down a lot of the time, but “sad or hopeless most of the day” feels… I don’t know, it feels like a very specific thing.

Some days I do feel kind of bleak, like I’m just moving through the day and everything feels harder than it should, but I don’t know if I’d call it sadness all day. It’s more like this heavy, gray feeling, like I’m not fully in anything. And hopeless… maybe in moments I think, “What if I don’t feel better?” but I don’t know if I’m sitting there feeling hopeless from morning to night.

It’s just been hard to tell what’s sadness and what’s being completely drained, if that makes sense.
When you rest, do you feel refreshed afterward?

No, not really. That’s actually kind of one of the main reasons I came in, because I keep thinking, okay, maybe I’m just tired, maybe if I lie down or sleep or take it easy for a bit I’ll reset, but I don’t.

Like after work, even if it’s not some huge dramatic shift, I’m so wiped out I can barely get through it. My body feels like it’s filled with wet sand, like every part of me is too heavy to move the normal way. And then I’ll rest, I’ll sit down, I’ll sleep, I’ll try not to do anything for a while, and afterward I might feel slightly less awful for a minute, but not refreshed. Not like, “Okay, I’m back.” It’s more like I’m still running on empty, just lying down while doing it.

It’s frustrating because resting is supposed to help, and it feels like it barely touches it.
How long have you been feeling this exhausted?

It’s been long enough that it stopped feeling like just a bad day or a couple of rough shifts, if that makes sense. I don’t know the exact day it started, but it’s been going on for a while now — enough that I came in because I’m so tired I can barely get through a normal shift.

Like, it’s not just after some huge effort. I’ll be at the register doing regular things, and by the end I feel completely emptied out. My body feels like it’s filled with wet sand, and then I’ll rest or sleep thinking I’ll come back from it, but I don’t really. I might feel a tiny bit less awful, but not actually restored.

So… I guess I’d say it’s been persistent, not just one or two days. It’s been hanging around and affecting my work enough that I couldn’t just ignore it anymore.
Has this exhaustion been going on for 6 months or longer?

I honestly don’t know if I can say six months or longer. I don’t want to give you a number and then have it be wrong, because it’s kind of blurred together.

What I do know is that I came in because I’m so tired I can barely get through a shift. It’s not just normal tired, like needing a nap after work. It’s this heavy, dragging feeling, like my body is filled with wet sand, and even when I rest it doesn’t really bring me back. I’ll lie down or sleep or sit still for a while, and I still feel like I’m running on empty.

So… six months, I’m not sure. It’s been persistent enough that it’s interfering with work, but I can’t confidently say it’s been that long.
Did this start after a flu-like illness or infection?

I’m not really sure. I’ve been trying to think back on that, because it feels like there should be some clear “before and after,” like I got sick and then never bounced back, but I can’t honestly point to anything like that.

I mean, I get little colds or feel run-down sometimes like anybody, especially being around people at work all day, but I don’t remember a specific flu or infection where afterward this exhaustion clearly started. It’s more like… it crept up, or at least that’s how it feels to me now. I might be missing something, but nothing stands out in my mind as, “Oh, that was the illness that triggered it.”
Have you been feeling nervous or worried a lot lately?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I get worried about normal things, like whether I’m going to make it through work okay or if I’m going to mess something up because I’m so tired, but I don’t know if I’d call it nervous all the time.

It’s more like… I’m aware of how bad I feel, and then I start thinking about it, and that can make me uneasy. But I haven’t really been keeping track of it as “anxiety” or anything. I don’t wake up and think, “I’m nervous today,” if that makes sense. It’s just kind of mixed in with everything else, and I’m not sure what’s what anymore.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things on most days?

I don’t think I can say “excessively” on most days, no… or at least I’m not sure that’s what’s happening. I do worry, but it feels tied to whatever is right in front of me, like getting through the day or whether I’m going to be able to keep up with things. It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting around worrying about every possible thing all day long.

But then again, I don’t always know where the line is, you know? Like, what counts as normal worry versus excessive worry. Sometimes if I’m already worn down, even small things feel bigger than they probably are, and I can get stuck thinking about them for a bit. But I wouldn’t say I’m worried most days about a bunch of different things for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way.
Over the last two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day, no. I mean… I’ve had days where I feel pretty low, especially when I’m tired or when the day just feels like too much, but I haven’t really been tracking it like that, like counting the days or anything.

Sometimes I think I’m more frustrated or worn out than depressed, if that makes sense. Like I’ll feel heavy or discouraged, but then other times I’m just trying to get through work and do what I’m supposed to do, and I don’t really stop to label it. So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean like a constant depressed mood almost every day for two weeks, because I’m not sure that’s been happening.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t really like saying that out loud, but yes, I’ve had thoughts like that.

It’s not like I’m sitting there making some big plan all the time, but there have been these really scary moments where I think, like… maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Like if I could just disappear without having to deal with anything or make anybody deal with me. And I know that sounds awful, and then I feel guilty even thinking it.

And a few times when I was on my way home, I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic. It kind of scared me because it felt like the thought just showed up, and then I was like, “Why did I just think that?” I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it has happened.
Over the last two weeks, have you noticed a clear drop in your appetite?

Yeah… I think so. It’s been kind of up and down, honestly, so it’s hard for me to give a neat answer, but lately it’s mostly been that I just don’t really eat unless I suddenly realize I haven’t.

Like I’ll go through most of the day at work and then notice I only had coffee or maybe a few bites of something, and it’s not always on purpose. Food just doesn’t sound good, or when I do try to eat, it tastes kind of… flat, like cardboard almost. Even stuff I usually like doesn’t really do anything for me.

And I did notice my work pants are fitting looser. I haven’t been weighing myself every day or anything, so I don’t know exactly how much, but I can feel it when I’m getting dressed. So yes, I guess there has been a drop, at least recently.
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I’ve definitely had times where things just felt kind of empty for a while. I don’t know if I can neatly separate “depressed” from just… losing interest in everything, but that’s usually how I notice it first.

Like, things I usually really love — cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place — they start to feel flat. Like I’m doing them because I know I’m supposed to like them, or because that’s what I normally do, but there’s no real feeling behind it. It’s like I’m pretending to care, and then I feel weird because I know those things used to matter to me.

So yes, I think before this current stretch, I’ve had periods like that that lasted at least a couple weeks. It’s not always dramatic from the outside, but inside it feels like everything gets muted.
During that earlier period you mentioned, did it feel separate from what you’re going through now, like there was a time in between when you had gotten back to your usual self?

I’m honestly not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. I think there were times in between where I seemed more normal, or at least I was functioning better and not thinking about it as much. Like I could get through work, talk to people, do regular stuff, and I probably would’ve said I was “fine” if somebody asked.

But I don’t know if I got all the way back to my usual self, if that makes sense. Sometimes it feels like it fades into the background more than it completely goes away. So… yes, maybe it was separate in the sense that this current thing feels like its own stretch, but I’m not confident about where one period ended and the next one started. It all kind of blends together when I try to look back at it.
Between that earlier period and how you feel now, was there a time when you felt back to your normal self?

I don’t know if I can say that for sure. There were stretches where I was doing better, definitely — like I’d go to work, keep up with things, talk to people more normally, and I wasn’t sitting there thinking, “Something is wrong with me” every day.

But “back to my normal self” feels harder to pin down. I think maybe I had times where I felt close to it, or at least I could ignore how off I felt because life was moving along. But when I look back, it’s kind of blurry. I can’t confidently point to a chunk of time and say, yes, I was completely myself again before this started.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. There may have been a period where I seemed okay from the outside, but I don’t know if I really felt fully normal inside.
Was there ever a time between the earlier period and now when you felt completely back to your usual self?

I don’t think I can honestly say “completely,” no. Like, there were definitely times where I was more functional, and if you’d seen me from the outside you might’ve thought I was back to normal. I’d be going to work, doing errands, answering texts more, not just completely checked out.

But inside, I don’t know… it’s hard for me to separate “I’m okay enough to get through the day” from “I’m actually back to myself.” Those feel different to me. I think I had stretches where things were quieter or less heavy, but I’m not sure there was a clear point where I felt fully like me again.

So I guess my answer is: maybe somewhat better at times, but completely back to my usual self? I’m not sure I ever really felt confident saying that.
At any point between that earlier period and now, did you feel completely back to your usual self?

I know I keep kind of circling around it, but… no, I don’t think I can say there was a point where I felt completely back to my usual self. Not in a clear, confident way.

There were times where I was more okay on the outside, if that makes sense. Like I could get through my shifts, make conversation, do the normal routine, and maybe even think, “Okay, things are settling down.” But when you ask “completely back,” that feels like a higher bar, and I don’t know that I ever really hit that.

It’s hard because when you’re in it, you’re not always measuring yourself every day. You just keep going, and then later you try to look back and figure out, “Was I normal then? Was that me feeling better, or was I just managing?” And I honestly can’t tell. I think I had better stretches, quieter stretches, but not a time where I would say I felt fully like myself again.
Between that earlier period and now, was there any time when you felt fully back to your normal self?

I’m sorry, I know I’ve sort of answered this a few different ways already. I think the most honest answer is no — or at least, not that I can clearly remember and point to.

There were times where I was doing more normal things, and maybe I looked more like myself from the outside. Like I could get through work, talk to people without it being obvious something was off, keep up with basic stuff. But feeling fully back to normal… I don’t know. That’s where I get stuck.

It’s like there’s “functioning” and then there’s actually feeling like me, and I don’t think those were always the same thing. I had stretches where I was closer, or where things weren’t as intense, but I can’t say there was a clean period where I felt completely back to my usual self. I wish I could give you a simpler yes or no, but if I’m being careful, I’d say no, not fully.
Was there ever a period of at least 2 months when you were not feeling depressed or uninterested in things?

I don’t think so, no. At least not a full two months where I felt like I was really interested in things again.

It’s not like every single minute is exactly the same, but the bigger pattern has been that things I normally care about just feel… flat. Like cooking for myself — I used to actually enjoy planning something and making it, even if it was simple. Or playing guitar, or going hiking, or going over to my family’s place. Those are things that usually feel like “me,” you know? But lately I’ll try to do them and it’s like I’m going through the motions, like I’m pretending to care because I know I’m supposed to care.

There might have been days here and there where it was a little lighter, or I could distract myself for a bit, but if you mean two months where I wasn’t depressed or where I actually had my interest back in things, I don’t think I’ve had that. Not really.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about excessive worry/anxiety on most days, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific anxiety or excessive-worry symptom item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I can say “excessively” on most days, no… or at least I’m not sure that’s what’s happening. I do worry, but it feels tied to whatever is right in front of me, like getting through the day or whether I’m going to be able to keep up with things. It doesn’t feel like I’m sitting around worrying about every possible thing all day long.

But then again, I don’t always know where the line is, you know? Like, what counts as normal worry versus excessive worry. Sometimes if I’m already worn down, even small things feel bigger than they probably are, and I can get stuck thinking about them for a bit. But I wouldn’t say I’m worried most days about a bunch of different things for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed it that way.

inference.note: Anxiety symptoms are not prominent, making F41.9 less likely. Duration remains unclear and below-confidence for G93.3/CFS, so that is deprioritized. Persistent fatigue with reduced interest/low mood still supports depressive episode vs recurrent depression, with neurasthenia and nonspecific fatigue remaining in the differential.

doctor.intent: Differentiate major depressive disorder from fatigue/neurasthenia by determining whether low mood is present nearly every day.
doctor.question: Over the last two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about depressed mood nearly every day over the last two weeks, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific depressed mood item.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day, no. I mean… I’ve had days where I feel pretty low, especially when I’m tired or when the day just feels like too much, but I haven’t really been tracking it like that, like counting the days or anything.

Sometimes I think I’m more frustrated or worn out than depressed, if that makes sense. Like I’ll feel heavy or discouraged, but then other times I’m just trying to get through work and do what I’m supposed to do, and I don’t really stop to label it. So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say yes if you mean like a constant depressed mood almost every day for two weeks, because I’m not sure that’s been happening.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the patient has passive thoughts of death or suicidal ideation, which is critical for safety and also helps distinguish a depressive episode from fatigue-related conditions.
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I’ve had scary thoughts like maybe everyone would be better off if I didn’t wake up, and a few times on the way home I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about thoughts of being better off dead, which matches recurrent thoughts of death or suicidal ideation.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I don’t really like saying that out loud, but yes, I’ve had thoughts like that.

It’s not like I’m sitting there making some big plan all the time, but there have been these really scary moments where I think, like… maybe everyone would be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Like if I could just disappear without having to deal with anything or make anybody deal with me. And I know that sounds awful, and then I feel guilty even thinking it.

And a few times when I was on my way home, I caught myself thinking about stepping off the curb into traffic. It kind of scared me because it felt like the thought just showed up, and then I was like, “Why did I just think that?” I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but it has happened.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has a core major depressive symptom that would distinguish depressive disorder from fatigue/neurasthenia: impaired appetite.

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: My appetite has been all over the place, but lately I mostly forget to eat or food tastes like cardboard, and my work pants have been fitting looser.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking directly about a drop in appetite over the last two weeks, which matches the appetite/weight change symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think so. It’s been kind of up and down, honestly, so it’s hard for me to give a neat answer, but lately it’s mostly been that I just don’t really eat unless I suddenly realize I haven’t.

Like I’ll go through most of the day at work and then notice I only had coffee or maybe a few bites of something, and it’s not always on purpose. Food just doesn’t sound good, or when I do try to eat, it tastes kind of… flat, like cardboard almost. Even stuff I usually like doesn’t really do anything for me.

And I did notice my work pants are fitting looser. I haven’t been weighing myself every day or anything, so I don’t know exactly how much, but I can feel it when I’m getting dressed. So yes, I guess there has been a drop, at least recently.

inference.note: Suicidal thoughts and decreased appetite/weight loss strengthen a depressive episode; anxiety/neurasthenia and nonspecific fatigue are less likely, so F48.0 and R53 are dropped.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a past depressive episode to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode.
doctor.question: Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: Things I usually love, like cooking for myself, playing guitar, hiking, or going to my family’s place, just feel flat now, like I’m only pretending to care.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about any prior depressive episode characterized by depressed mood or loss of interest lasting at least two weeks; the closest symptom profile item directly covering this is loss of interest.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I’ve definitely had times where things just felt kind of empty for a while. I don’t know if I can neatly separate “depressed” from just… losing interest in everything, but that’s usually how I notice it first.

Like, things I usually really love — cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place — they start to feel flat. Like I’m doing them because I know I’m supposed to like them, or because that’s what I normally do, but there’s no real feeling behind it. It’s like I’m pretending to care, and then I feel weird because I know those things used to matter to me.

So yes, I think before this current stretch, I’ve had periods like that that lasted at least a couple weeks. It’s not always dramatic from the outside, but inside it feels like everything gets muted.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a prior distinct major depressive episode, which would distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode.
doctor.question: During that earlier period you mentioned, did it feel separate from what you’re going through now, like there was a time in between when you had gotten back to your usual self?

target_item.reason: The question is asking whether a prior depressive period was distinct from the current one with a return to usual functioning in between, but the provided symptom profiles do not include an item covering episode separation or interepisode recovery.

patient.answer:
I’m honestly not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. I think there were times in between where I seemed more normal, or at least I was functioning better and not thinking about it as much. Like I could get through work, talk to people, do regular stuff, and I probably would’ve said I was “fine” if somebody asked.

But I don’t know if I got all the way back to my usual self, if that makes sense. Sometimes it feels like it fades into the background more than it completely goes away. So… yes, maybe it was separate in the sense that this current thing feels like its own stretch, but I’m not confident about where one period ended and the next one started. It all kind of blends together when I try to look back at it.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a distinct period of recovery between past depressive symptoms and the current episode, to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single current depressive episode.
doctor.question: Between that earlier period and how you feel now, was there a time when you felt back to your normal self?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there was a period of return to normal functioning between depressive periods, which is about episode separation/remission; the provided symptom profiles do not include a specific item for that.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I can say that for sure. There were stretches where I was doing better, definitely — like I’d go to work, keep up with things, talk to people more normally, and I wasn’t sitting there thinking, “Something is wrong with me” every day.

But “back to my normal self” feels harder to pin down. I think maybe I had times where I felt close to it, or at least I could ignore how off I felt because life was moving along. But when I look back, it’s kind of blurry. I can’t confidently point to a chunk of time and say, yes, I was completely myself again before this started.

So… I guess the honest answer is I’m not sure. There may have been a period where I seemed okay from the outside, but I don’t know if I really felt fully normal inside.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a clear period of full remission between depressive episodes to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single depressive episode.
doctor.question: Was there ever a time between the earlier period and now when you felt completely back to your usual self?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there was a full return to usual baseline functioning between episodes, which is not directly covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I can honestly say “completely,” no. Like, there were definitely times where I was more functional, and if you’d seen me from the outside you might’ve thought I was back to normal. I’d be going to work, doing errands, answering texts more, not just completely checked out.

But inside, I don’t know… it’s hard for me to separate “I’m okay enough to get through the day” from “I’m actually back to myself.” Those feel different to me. I think I had stretches where things were quieter or less heavy, but I’m not sure there was a clear point where I felt fully like me again.

So I guess my answer is: maybe somewhat better at times, but completely back to my usual self? I’m not sure I ever really felt confident saying that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was full remission between episodes to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single depressive episode.
doctor.question: At any point between that earlier period and now, did you feel completely back to your usual self?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether there was a full return to baseline between episodes, which is about episode separation/remission rather than any specific symptom profile item listed.

patient.answer:
I know I keep kind of circling around it, but… no, I don’t think I can say there was a point where I felt completely back to my usual self. Not in a clear, confident way.

There were times where I was more okay on the outside, if that makes sense. Like I could get through my shifts, make conversation, do the normal routine, and maybe even think, “Okay, things are settling down.” But when you ask “completely back,” that feels like a higher bar, and I don’t know that I ever really hit that.

It’s hard because when you’re in it, you’re not always measuring yourself every day. You just keep going, and then later you try to look back and figure out, “Was I normal then? Was that me feeling better, or was I just managing?” And I honestly can’t tell. I think I had better stretches, quieter stretches, but not a time where I would say I felt fully like myself again.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a distinct period of full remission between the earlier depressive episode and the current one to differentiate recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode.
doctor.question: Between that earlier period and now, was there any time when you felt fully back to your normal self?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about whether there was a return to baseline or a symptom-free interval between periods, which is not directly covered by any listed symptom profile item.

patient.answer:
I’m sorry, I know I’ve sort of answered this a few different ways already. I think the most honest answer is no — or at least, not that I can clearly remember and point to.

There were times where I was doing more normal things, and maybe I looked more like myself from the outside. Like I could get through work, talk to people without it being obvious something was off, keep up with basic stuff. But feeling fully back to normal… I don’t know. That’s where I get stuck.

It’s like there’s “functioning” and then there’s actually feeling like me, and I don’t think those were always the same thing. I had stretches where I was closer, or where things weren’t as intense, but I can’t say there was a clean period where I felt completely back to my usual self. I wish I could give you a simpler yes or no, but if I’m being careful, I’d say no, not fully.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a symptom-free remission of at least 2 months between depressive episodes, to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single episode that never fully remitted.
doctor.question: Was there ever a period of at least 2 months when you were not feeling depressed or uninterested in things?

target_item.name: Loss_of_Interest
target_item.manifestation: Things I usually love, like cooking for myself, playing guitar, hiking, or going to my family’s place, just feel flat now, like I’m only pretending to care.
target_item.reason: The question asks whether there was a sustained period of at least 2 months without feeling depressed or uninterested in things; the most directly covered profile item is loss of interest/anhedonia.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so, no. At least not a full two months where I felt like I was really interested in things again.

It’s not like every single minute is exactly the same, but the bigger pattern has been that things I normally care about just feel… flat. Like cooking for myself — I used to actually enjoy planning something and making it, even if it was simple. Or playing guitar, or going hiking, or going over to my family’s place. Those are things that usually feel like “me,” you know? But lately I’ll try to do them and it’s like I’m going through the motions, like I’m pretending to care because I know I’m supposed to care.

There might have been days here and there where it was a little lighter, or I could distract myself for a bit, but if you mean two months where I wasn’t depressed or where I actually had my interest back in things, I don’t think I’ve had that. Not really.
